# Regrans

<!-- badges: start -->

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/RafaelMotaAlvess/Regrans/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/RafaelMotaAlvess/Regrans/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![License: GPL-3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPL--3-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html)

<!-- badges: end -->

## Overview

Regrans helps you explore data whose relationship changes across the range of an explanatory variable. Choose two independent lines that may jump, or two lines that meet at an estimated breakpoint. Both options search for one transition by minimizing residual sum of squares. You can inspect the fitted lines and edit the resulting plot.

## Installation

Regrans is not on CRAN yet. Install the latest tagged version from GitHub:

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("RafaelMotaAlvess/Regrans@v0.1.0")
```

For the development version, omit `@v0.1.0`; it requires R 4.1 or newer. The [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/RafaelMotaAlvess/Regrans/releases) page also provides a source package and Windows and macOS binaries. The [installation guide](docs/installation.md) explains how to choose and install one.

## Usage

```r
library(Regrans)

observations <- data.frame(x = 1:20)
observations$y <- ifelse(observations$x <= 10,
                         2 + observations$x,
                         -15 + 3 * observations$x) +
  sin(observations$x) / 5

fit <- regrans(y ~ x, data = observations)
fit$location               # selected interval between observed x values
fit$segments               # intercept and slope of each line
tidy(fit)                  # coefficients with conditional statistics
glance(fit)                # model, location, and fit score
plot_regrans(fit, pch = 16) # editable ggplot2 graphic

continuous_fit <- regrans(y ~ x, data = observations,
                          model = "continuous")
continuous_fit$location$estimate
plot_regrans(continuous_fit)
```

The default `"discontinuous"` fit permits a jump and reports an interval, not a numeric breakpoint. The `"continuous"` fit joins the lines at an estimated point. If the continuous profile is numerically flat, `location$status` is `"unidentified"` and a single linear fit is returned. `augment(fit)` adds fitted values, residuals, and segment labels to the original rows. See the [usage guide](docs/usage.md) for data requirements and interpretation.
